newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds Metals to begin lay offs in June.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds Metals to begin lay offs in June.

text.p: Reynolds Metals Co is to begin laying off large numbers of staff at the company's corporate head office in Richmond, VA. this month, and may shut its Alabama plant prior to selloff, analysts and industry sources said.
Up to 500 staff were being laid off at the head office, industry sources said. "Middle management has been hit hard," one observer said.

Reynolds spokeswoman Lou Ann Nabhan said that, as previously announced, the company has restructured into six new units which are now being staffed and it was too soon to say how many jobs would be affected.
"We expect there will be lay offs during the month of June," Nabhan said. She added that any estimates of redundancies were pure speculation.
Some 1,800 people are in corporate head office jobs, Nabhan said.
Reynolds has been selling several businesses in a bid to steer the company onto a more profitable route.

The company's Alabama rolling mill is being sold to Alcoa, but observers said it will be handed over as a shut plant with Reynolds absorbing the write-offs associated with lay offs, which could total up to 500 people.
"We don't have knowledge of this. It's pure speculation," Nabhan said, referring to possible closure of the Alabama plant before handover.
Analyst Victor Lazarovici of Smith Barney said Reynolds was in a "severe cutting" mode.
Industry eyebrows were raised when Kaiser Aluminum backed out of talks to buy Reynolds' McCook, Ill. sheet and plate plant.

"The Kaiser deal falling off the rails was a clear indication they had a few problems to deal with," Lazarovici said, adding there was less than a 50:50 chance Reynolds would meet the self-imposed end of June deadline for its portfolio review or new company structure.
Nabhan said an update on the review would be given with second quarter results on July 16. "We are on track with the portfolio review," she added.
Reynolds' CEO Jeremiah Sheehan told reporters at Alumitech in Atlanta last month the company may not meet the June deadline for the review.
